note: Read 2026-10-31 on Laws of Bangladesh (bdlaws.minlaw.gov.bd, the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division). Its pages are served in UTF-16; each was saved as served and re-encoded to UTF-8, unchanged otherwise, for the check (files bd-maj3, bd-la2, bd-la34). Majority: The Majority Act, 1875 (Act No. IX of 1875), s. 3: a person domiciled in Bangladesh attains majority on completing eighteen; a minor with a court-appointed guardian of person or property (or under a Court of Wards) only at twenty-one, which the form doesn't hold. Personal-law matters (marriage, dower, divorce, adoption) are saved by s. 2 (not held). Work: বাংলাদেশ শ্রম আইন, ২০০৬ (Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, Act No. 42 of 2006, as amended), s. 2(63): a child (শিশু) is a person who hasn't completed fourteen; s. 34(1): no child may be employed or allowed to work in any occupation or establishment; s. 34(2): an adolescent (fourteen to seventeen) only with a registered doctor's certificate of fitness held by the employer and a token carried at work (not held). Performers: the Act has no exception for performers, so 'barred' is held as the Act's words; whether children's work in film and television falls within an 'establishment' under the Act, and any rule of the Children Act 2013, weren't read; a reading to check. Service: Service is held null: no source saying no service is asked was reached today (the blocker file names the attempts); a reading only, not held: Bangladesh has no conscription (no source saved).

sources.title: The Majority Act, 1875, section 3 (Laws of Bangladesh)
sources.said: Subject as aforesaid, every other person domiciled in Bangladesh shall be deemed to have attained his majority when he shall have completed his age of eighteen years and not before.
